key_insight: Automated model discovery identified a sparse, three-term hyperelastic law for TPU-coated woven nylon, combining one isotropic and two anisotropic contributions.
engineering_relevance: The discovered law can support finite-element simulations of fabric-based structures, including soft robotic devices.
method: Fit Constitutive Artificial Neural Networks to biaxial test data to jointly discover the material law and its parameters.
Assess predictive robustness across 20 network initializations.
Use LARS-LASSO to independently identify dominant constitutive contributions.
evidence_signal: The discovered law reproduced measured biaxial responses with mean R² = 0.97, while LARS-LASSO recovered the same dominant contributions at approximately 100-fold lower computational cost.
watch_item: Correlated candidate terms yielded different sparse representations across initializations, so robust predictions do not establish a unique constitutive law.
paper_title: Unweaving the mechanics of woven fabrics through automated model discovery
